newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan markets seen unaffected on Friday by Deng.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan markets seen unaffected on Friday by Deng.

text.p: Taiwan's stock market is expected to continue climbing on Friday while the local dollar is likely to fall further against the U.S. currency in the wake of the death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
However, financial analysts said both markets are likely to ignore much of the aftermath to Deng's death and instead move according to economic forces.
"Unless communist China announces some sort of big policy change, Deng's death is no longer a major factor in Taiwan's markets," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust Co.
Shrugging off political concerns after Beijing announced that Deng had died late Wednesday night, Taiwan's stock market closed 21.19 points or 0.28 percent higher at 7,678.04.
The index, buoyed by widspread expectation of an economic recovery in 1997, has finished higher in 12 of the past 14 sessions and gained more than 500 points during that span.
The Taiwan dollar suffered some post-Deng selling on Thursday, closing lower against the greeback at T$27.625 compared to Wednesday's T$27.583 finish.

But dealers said safe-haven buying of the U.S. dollar was only a small factor in the local currency's fall while the primary cause was the greenback's persistent strength overseas against other major currencies.
"Even before Deng's death the Taiwan dollar was already in a downtrend due to the U.S. dollar's strength in overseas markets," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"The Taiwan dollar is likely to fall again tomorrow (Friday) mainly because of the U.S. dollar strength, not because of Deng's death," she said.
Rumours that Deng's health was failing first hit the stock market on Tuesday and caused a mild sell-off during that session.

But the index rebounded sharply on Wednesday and continued to gain on Thursday as investors showed they no longer feared political chaos would grip China following its patriarch's death, analysts said.

"(China's President) Jiang Zemin pretty much has solidified his power base, at least for the short term, so investors are not worried about any instability that might affect Taiwan," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust Co.
Brokers have predicted that the stock market would soar past the 8,000-point level by the end of March on the strength of a recovery economy.

The economy received a further boost on Thursday when the government announced Taiwan's gross domestic product grew a relatively high 6.62 percent in the fourth quarter, bringing full-year 1996 growth to 5.71 percent.
The central bank has forecast a 1997 GDP growth of 6.17 percent.
Analysts predicted ranges of T$27.60-68 and 7,650-7,730 respectively for the Taiwan dollar and the stock index for Friday.
